name: Diagonal Collar (Calendar Collar)
summary: Long 100 shares, a longer-dated protective put, and a shorter-dated covered call sold repeatedly against the stock; a collar whose protection outlives each income leg.

legs.strike_rule: 100 shares per unit; the stock is the base of the structure.
Protective put by delta |0.20-0.35|, typically 5-10% below the share cost basis.
Covered call by delta 0.20-0.30, strike ABOVE the share cost basis so a called-away outcome is profitable.
legs.dte_rule: front expiry, 21-45 DTE, re-sold each cycle

max_profit: (Short call strike - share cost basis) x 100 - net option debit + cumulative call credits collected, if the shares are called away at the short strike.
max_loss: (Share cost basis - long put strike) x 100 + net option debit - cumulative credits, if the stock collapses below the put strike. Fully defined for as long as the put is held.
breakevens: Share cost basis + net option debit per share - cumulative credits per share.

greeks.delta: net positive +0.45 to +0.75 per unit (stock 1.00 minus put ~0.28 minus call ~0.25)
greeks.theta: positive once the put's decay is outpaced by the rolled call credits; negative in the first cycle
greeks.vega: net positive - the long-dated put has more vega than the short front call

when_to_use: When the account already holds (or wants to hold) 100 shares of a quality underlying and wants both downside protection and income, with the protection deliberately outliving each income cycle. Buy the long-dated put when IV rank < 30; sell the calls when front-month IV is rich. Best on dividend-paying large caps and ETFs where the dividend partially finances the put - but note that dividends raise the short call's early-assignment risk.
typical_dte: put 90-365 DTE, call 21-45 DTE rolled monthly
entry_rules: Own or simultaneously buy exactly 100 shares per unit.
IV rank < 30 at the time of the protective put purchase.
Protective put delta |0.20-0.35|, DTE 90-365; cost of the put <= 4% of the share position value.
Short call delta 0.20-0.30, DTE 21-45, strike strictly above the share cost basis.
Net option debit (put cost - call credit) <= 2% of the share position value per cycle.
Share position value per unit <= 20% of account equity ($10,000 on a $50k account).
LEVEL 3 OK (level 1/2 would in fact suffice: covered call plus long protective put). Submit as separate orders: buy shares, buy put, then sell call. Always own the shares BEFORE selling the call.
management_rules: Close the short call at 50-75% of its credit and re-sell the next 21-45 DTE cycle at delta 0.20-0.30.

If the short call's |delta| exceeds 0.60 and the shares are at risk of being called away at a profit, either let it happen (it is a profitable outcome) or roll up and out for a net credit - never for a debit.
Roll the protective put down and out when its DTE < 60, capturing remaining value and re-establishing at delta |0.20-0.35|.

If the stock closes below the put strike, evaluate exercising the put versus selling the shares and the put separately - selling the put in the market almost always captures more value than exercising it.
Never sell a call at a strike below the share cost basis; that locks in a loss on a called-away outcome.
exit_rules: Close or roll the short call by 14:30 ET on its expiration day if it is ITM and being called away is not the desired outcome; if being called away IS acceptable and profitable, this is the one structure in the family where assignment may be allowed to occur deliberately - but the automation must confirm (short strike > cost basis) before permitting it.
Close the short call immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05 and being called away is NOT desired.
Close the short call before the session preceding ex-dividend if its extrinsic < the dividend per share and you intend to keep the shares and the dividend.
Never sell the protective put while holding the shares unless the entire position is being unwound on the same ticket.
Full exit order: buy back the short call, then sell the shares, then sell the put.
assignment_risk: The short call, assigned against shares you actually own - the mildest case in the family, since it simply sells the stock at the strike. This is the one structure where assignment can be an acceptable exit rather than a failure, provided the short strike exceeds the cost basis. Ex-dividend remains the dominant early-exercise trigger, and a call assigned the day before the ex-date costs you the dividend.
buying_power: Cost of the 100 shares (or 50% on margin) plus the net option debit. The short call is covered by shares; the long put adds no requirement.
liquidity_needs: Long-dated puts 90-365 DTE need OI >= 200 and spread <= 6% of mid. Underlying ADV >= 2M shares. Restrict to large caps and major ETFs.
common_mistakes: Selling a call below the cost basis; letting the protective put decay inside 60 DTE without rolling; exercising the put instead of selling it; treating a called-away outcome as a failure when it was profitable; forgetting the dividend when the short call is ITM before an ex-date.
zero_dte_notes: The short call leg could be sold weekly but never at 0DTE under this playbook; the shares make assignment survivable, but weekly gamma is not worth the premium.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
